anf_compare.notes: ANF has no text of this homily; translated directly from the PG 93 Greek.

bible_refs.note: ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν βασιλευόντων matches 1 Timothy 6:15 word for word; cited inline in Pass B beside the clause.

choices.why: Takes up the homily's earlier theme of the unlettered fishermen (u01-rem-close). Acts 4:13 calls Peter and John ἀγράμματοι; the epithet is traditional here, so it stays a possible echo, not an inline citation.
The net from above, playing on 'fishers of men'; Matthew 13:47 is a possible echo only.
ὄψον is cooked food eaten with bread, very often fish; 'choice fare' keeps the image without a calque.

choices.english: the Master's table, at which … dines
rejected: the lordly table which he dines
choices.why: The Master is Christ, so capitalised; the accusative of the table is rendered 'at which … dines'.

rejected: to the ages of the ages
choices.why: Standard English form of the doxology; the literal form is a calque.

pass_a_gloss: [continuing the exhortation of u02-rem-mid: '…let us escape and'] let us become, of Christ's unlettered apostles, fishes of the net above, relishes of the Master's table, which the King of those who reign dines on, holding our salvation [to be] food; to him [be] the glory and the might into the ages of the ages. Amen. [The trailing '5' is a page number of the print, not text.]
pass_b_english: …let us become fish in the heavenly net of Christ's unlettered apostles, choice fare for the Master's table, at which the King of kings (1 Timothy 6:15) dines, counting our salvation as his food. To him be glory and might for ever and ever. Amen.
source_text:
γενώμεθα Χριστοῦ ἀγραμμάτων ἀποστόλων ἰχθύες τῆς ἄνω σαγήνης, ὄψα τῆς
δεσποτικῆς τραπέζης ἣν ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν βασιλευόντων δειπνεῖ βρῶσιν τὴν ἡμετέραν
σωτηρίαν ἡγούμενος· αὐτῷ ἡ δόξα καὶ τὸ κράτος εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων.
Ἀμήν.

5
source_normalizations: Trailing '5' in the source block is a page number from the print, not text; not translated.
notes: The row begins mid-sentence: γενώμεθα continues the hortatory subjunctives of u02-rem-mid (ἐκφύγωμεν … ἐκκλίνωμεν … ἐκφύγωμεν καὶ), whose English ends '…waves, and…'; this row opens '…let us become' so the conjunction is not repeated.
βρῶσιν τὴν ἡμετέραν σωτηρίαν ἡγούμενος may recall John 4:34, but the wording differs, so it is not cited inline.
The doxology is the standard homily close (compare 1 Peter 4:11; Revelation 1:6) and is treated as a liturgical formula, not cited inline.

review.coverage: every clause checked against the source
changes: removed a repeated opening 'and' that already ends u02-rem-mid
'to the ages of ages' -> 'for ever and ever'
translator note now points to u01-rem-close for the unlettered-fishermen theme
